issues.issue: The recital states that term loan lenders "shall provide" approximately US$530,000,000 and Project financing of US$713,000,000, while the operative "Total Commitment" definition fixes the commitment at US$250,000,000 and Section 2.20 makes any Accession Project Financing wholly discretionary. A court could be asked whether the recital creates an obligation the operative text does not.

"[A]ny material property or assets" sets no threshold, so the date on which the Borrower's additional-collateral obligations are triggered has no ascertainable boundary. The word "material" is undefined anywhere in Section 1.01.

The closing condition "on the same terms as the required by the Loans" is grammatically incomplete, leaving unclear what comparison of prepayment terms triggers inclusion of items (ii) and (iii) in the denominator. The whole pro rata fraction turns on that clause.

The definition closes each limb with "in each case to the extent arising in connection with the Additional Obligations", defining the term by reference to itself. The circularity leaves the outer boundary of the secured Additional Obligations undetermined.

The definition ends with an open catch-all — "each other security agreement or other security instrument or document executed and delivered to the reasonable satisfaction of the Security Agent" — after a list of specific document types. Its reach against the enumerated specifics is uncertain.

"Agents" is defined to include the Intercreditor Agent, but the "Intercreditor Agent" definition contemplates that no such agent may ever be appointed and the "Common Project Financing Facility" definition says an Intercreditor Agreement is only permissive. Whether "Agents" obligations bind a non-existent party is left open.

"Borrowing" is defined as "(a) a Term Loan or (b) an LC Exposure", equating a loan with an exposure amount rather than a credit extension. That mismatch makes provisions keyed to a "Borrowing" (minimum size, Borrowing Request, Interest Period) hard to apply to limb (b).

The phrase "commercial banks in the Hibbing, Minnesota, New York, New York, and Singapore are authorized or required by law to remain closed" is ungrammatical, and it is unclear whether closure in any one, or all, of the three centres suffices. The stray "the" and the missing conjunction leave the test unfixed.

Cash counts only if held at institutions "acceptable to the Lenders", a standard with no criteria and no reasonableness qualifier. Clause (c) also runs on with an unclosed parenthesis after "the Security Documents".

"Cash Available" and "Cash Sweep Cash Available" use the identical five components but only the latter carries the "without double counting" opener and the maintenance-capex deduction. Whether the DSCR and the Cash Sweep DSCR are meant to measure the same cash is left unresolved.

The definition adds "scheduled repayments of Loans to Project Lenders" to "corresponding scheduled repayments of any Supplier Financing", but the Recitals define "Project Lenders" to include the providers of supplier's credit. Read with that recital definition the supplier debt is counted twice.

The First Sweep Period mechanism operates "for each Sweep Date occurring in such period", but "Sweep Date" requires a full fiscal quarter within the period and "First Sweep Period" (nine months after a Scheduled Commercial Operations Date that may be as late as 30 June 2013, to 1 April 2014) may contain none. On those definitions limb (i) can be a dead letter.

The parenthetical "(a \"Second Sweep Period Sweep Amount\")" is placed on the DSCR result in excess of 1.15 rather than on the fifty percent payment figure, so the defined term labels the wrong quantity. Limb (i) places the parallel label on the payment amount, so the two limbs define "Sweep Amount" differently.

Sweep Amounts are to be paid out of the DSRA to the extent the Escrow Account is short, yet the DSRA must be maintained at the Required Amount under Section 5.15 and is topped up as cash collateral under Section 2.06(j). Which obligation prevails on a deficient Sweep Payment Date is not stated.

The period runs from nine months after the Scheduled Commercial Operations Date to 1 April 2014, but "Scheduled Commercial Operations Date" may be as late as 30 June 2013, which would make the First Sweep Period a single day (or none at all). That cannot be squared with the First Sweep Period limb of the Cash Sweep Mechanism.

"[E]ach full fiscal quarter during the applicable Sweep Period" is unclear as to whether the quarter must fall wholly inside the Sweep Period or merely end during it. The result decides whether any Sweep Date arises in the short First Sweep Period.

The definition makes the Sweep Payment Date one Business Day after the last day of the quarter "in which a Sweep Date occurs", which pushes payment a full quarter after the measurement quarter; the worked example is needed to make the text intelligible. Whether the example or the words govern is arguable.

A Change in Control is triggered at "more than 49%" of voting Equity Interests, a threshold below control, and the carve-out "other than by EGL or its Affiliates" is undefined as to indirect acquisitions. The mismatch with an ordinary majority test invites argument.

The date depends on the Engineering Consultant certifying that "commercial production has commenced", a term nowhere defined and with no output or duration benchmark. Both limbs must occur, so the certification controls a date on which sweep and covenant tests turn.

The definition requires certification by "the Lenders' Engineering Consultant", a term that appears nowhere in Section 1.01; the defined party is the "Engineering Consultant". Whether they are the same person is left to inference.

The facility is described as one in which the Lenders "become a party" and which "may be subject to an Intercreditor Agreement", leaving both the mechanism of accession and the intercreditor arrangement optional and unspecified. The pari passu promise has no defined machinery behind it.

"Control" turns on the "power to direct or cause the direction of the management or policies of a Person ... by contract or otherwise", a formulation whose outer edge ("or otherwise") is undefined. It drives the Affiliate definition and the affiliate-transaction restrictions.

"[O]ther assets that are due, or likely to be converted into cash, sold, exchanged, or expensed in the normal course of business, within one (1) year" makes the class turn on the vague predicate "likely". The boundary matters because the Security Agreement subordinates the Lenders' lien over Current Assets.

Limb (c) captures "all scheduled amortization repayments of any other Indebtedness" although limbs (a) and (b) are finance charges and lease principal, so "other" has no clear antecedent. What debt service is actually counted is therefore uncertain.
